title: EEG recordings for semantic decoding of imagined animals and tools during auditory imagery task
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 7 participants performing an auditory imagery task, wherein subjects imagined sounds produced by objects from semantic categories (animals and tools) for 5-second intervals. Data were acquired using a BioSemi ActiveTwo system with 64 scalp electrodes, supplementary physiological channels including electrooculography, electrocardiography, and respiration monitoring, sampled at 2048 Hz. The dataset supports research in semantic brain-computer interfaces and neural decoding of imagined auditory content.
methods_description: EEG signals were recorded using a BioSemi ActiveTwo system with 64 electrodes positioned according to the international 10-20 system, plus bilateral earlobe reference electrodes. Electrooculography was recorded from four electrodes (vertical and horizontal placements around the right eye). Additional physiological measurements included wrist electrodes for heart rate variability and a respiration belt. Sampling rate was 2048 Hz.
